reasoning: 5x+4y=22, 3x+8y=30 -> 2*(eq1)=10x+8y=44, minus eq2 -> 7x=14, x=2 (y=3). KEPT '3': it is y, the wrong-variable answer (it is also plus-one of the key, the single relation left in the set). NEW '7': substitution slip - y=(22-5x)/4 into eq2 gives 3x+2(22-5x)=30; distributing the 2 only to the 22 gives 3x+44-5x=30 -> -2x=-14 -> x=7. y=4x-7 into ay-12x=-21 gives x(4a-12)=7a-21; infinitely many needs 4a-12=0 and 7a-21=0 -> a=3. KEPT '-3': cross-multiplying the coefficient proportion in the wrong direction (4a=-12) - the classic sign error here; the one remaining relation (negate). NEW '11': substituting the point (1,-3) and moving the -12 with the wrong sign: -3a-12=-21 read as -3a=-21-12=-33 -> a=11. NEW '-2.25': setting the x-coefficient condition but carrying the constant into it, 4a-12=-21 -> 4a=-9 -> a=-2.25. DROPPED square=9 and reciprocal=1/3.

5-2x>-3 -> -2x>-8 -> x<4; 4x+1>=-11 -> x>=-3. So -3<=x<4, greatest integer 3. KEPT '4': treating x<4 as x<=4 - the error the item is actually about (plus-one of the key, the single relation left). NEW '7': forgetting to divide by 2 when flipping, -2x>-8 -> x<8, greatest integer 7. NEW '0': misreading the first inequality's right side as +3, 5-2x>3 -> -2x>-2 -> x<1, greatest integer 0 (still within x>=-3). DROPPED negate=-3 (which was also just the lower bound) and minus-one=2. NOTE: my first attempt used -2 (sign slip on the 5); the relation checker rejected it because (-2)^2=4 would have added a second relation.

sqrt(x+6)=x -> x+6=x^2 -> x^2-x-6=0 -> x=3 or x=-2; -2 is extraneous. KEPT '−2': the extraneous root, the whole point of the item. NEW '2.95': completing the square on x^2-x=6 and forgetting to add 1/4 to the right side: (x-0.5)^2=6 -> x=0.5+2.449=2.95. NEW '7': misusing zero-product on the un-factored form x(x-1)=6, reading off 'x-1=6' -> x=7. DROPPED square=9 and double=6. This set has zero remaining derivation relations.

(a+b)/(a-b)=3 -> a+b=3a-3b -> 4b=2a -> a/b=2. KEPT '1/2': b/a, i.e. solving for the reciprocal ratio - the most common miss here; the single relation left in the set. NEW '-1': failing to distribute the minus, a+b=3a+3b -> -2b=2a -> a/b=-1. NEW '1/3': reporting the reciprocal of the GIVEN ratio, i.e. answering (a-b)/(a+b)=1/3 instead of a/b. DROPPED plus-one=3 and double=4. Note this stem has a small space of honest wrong values (1, -2, 3, 4 all collide with the key by a listed operation), which is why the two replacements are the ones above.

No solution needs 3/6=k/8 (and constants not matching): k=4. KEPT '16': inverting the proportion, k/8=6/3 -> k=16 - the single relation left (square). NEW '11.2': using the constants' ratio instead, 7/5=k/8 -> k=56/5=11.2; the same value falls out of substitution, y=(5-6x)/8 into eq1 gives x(24-6k)=56-5k and solving 56-5k=0 instead of 24-6k=0. NEW '2.25': writing eq1's slope upside down, -k/3=-3/4 -> k=9/4=2.25. DROPPED halve=2 and double=8.

9^x*3^(2x-1)=3^(4x-1); 27^(x+1)=3^(3x+3); 4x-1=3x+3 -> x=4. KEPT '2': failing to distribute the 3 on the right, 27^(x+1)->3^(3x+1), so 4x-1=3x+1 -> x=2; the single relation left (halve). NEW '1.5': reading 27 as 3^2, 4x-1=2x+2 -> x=1.5. NEW '1.69': multiplying exponents instead of adding when multiplying the powers, 2x(2x-1)=3x+3 -> 4x^2-5x-3=0 -> x=(5+sqrt(73))/8=1.69. DROPPED minus-one=3 and negate=-4.

f(g(a))=2(a^2+1)-3=2a^2-1=17 -> a^2=9 -> a=3. KEPT '9': stopping at a^2=9 and reporting it; the single relation left (square). KEPT '3.5' (never slip-derived): it is g(f(a))=17, (2a-3)^2+1=17 -> 2a-3=4 -> a=3.5, the composition-order error. NEW '3.16': dropping the +1 inside g, 2a^2-3=17 -> a^2=10 -> a=sqrt(10)=3.16. DROPPED plus-one=4.

Subtracting, (5x+3y)-(3x+5y)=15-1 -> 2x-2y=14 -> x-y=7. KEPT '14': stopping at 2x-2y=14 and forgetting to divide by 2; the single relation left (double). KEPT '4.5' (never slip-derived): it is x itself (adding gives x+y=2, so x=4.5, y=-2.5) - the wrong-quantity answer. NEW '2': adding instead of subtracting, 8x+8y=16 -> x+y=2. DROPPED negate=-7.

(x+y)^2=x^2+2xy+y^2 -> 25=17+2xy -> xy=4. KEPT '8': stopping at 2xy=8; the single relation left (double). KEPT '6' (never slip-derived): guessing the integers 3 and 2 that sum to 5 without checking x^2+y^2. NEW '6.25': assuming x=y=2.5 from x+y=5 and multiplying, 2.5*2.5=6.25. r+s=6, rs=k/2; r^2+s^2=36-k=22 -> k=14. KEPT '7': the product rs=7, i.e. forgetting that k=2rs; the single relation left (halve). KEPT '61' (never slip-derived): not dividing by the leading 2 at all - sum 12, product k, 144-2k=22 -> k=61. NEW '18': solving the wrong condition, the discriminant 144-8k=0 -> k=18. Solution: discriminant k^2-4(1)(9)=0 -> k^2=36 -> k=6. KEPT the original 36 (square slip) because it is the genuine error of solving k^2=36 and reporting k^2 instead of k. Dropped -6 (sign) and 3 (halve). NEW 10: student ignores the one-solution condition and just factors 9 over the integers as 9*1, giving sum of roots 9+1=10=k. Solution: a^(b+1)/a^b = a = 256/64 = 4. Dropped ALL three slip distractors (8 double, 2 halve, 16 square) because 8 and 16 chain into each other (8^2=64 would have created a second relation once 64 was added). NEW 3: solving for the wrong variable — with a=4, 4^b=64 gives b=3, and a student who finds b and stops reports 3. NEW 192: treating a^(b+1) as a^b + a, so 256 = 64 + a -> a = 192. NEW 64: reporting the given value a^b as if it were a. Remaining relations: 3 -> 4 (plus one) only.

Solution: 2^(3x) = 2^(2x+2) -> 3x = 2x+2 -> x = 2. KEPT the original 1 (halve) because it is exactly what a student gets by failing to distribute the exponent over (x+1): 3x = 2x+1 -> x=1. Dropped 4 (double) and 3 (plus one). NEW 0.67: taking logs and dividing rather than solving the linear equation, x = log4/log8 = 0.6021/0.9031 = 0.67. NEW 1.71: substituting the exponents for the bases (3^x = 2^(x+1)), giving x = log2/(log3-log2) = 0.3010/0.1761 = 1.71. Remaining relations: 1 -> 2 (double) only.

Solution: k^2 - 4(1)(16) = 0 -> k^2 = 64 -> k = 8. KEPT the original 4 (halve) because it is the classic dropped-coefficient error: setting k^2 = 16 instead of k^2 = 4*16 gives k = 4. Dropped -8 (sign) and 16 (double); 16 was also excluded because sqrt(16)=4 would have added a second relation. NEW 17: ignoring the one-solution condition and factoring 16 as 16*1, so k = 16+1 = 17. NEW 5.66: completing the square with 16 - k^2/2 = 0 instead of 16 - k^2/4 = 0, giving k = sqrt(32) = 5.66. Remaining relations: 4 -> 8 (double) only.

Solution: multiply by (x-2): x + 3(x-2) = 6 -> 4x - 6 = 6 -> x = 3. KEPT the original 2 (minus one) because it is the distribution error: x + 3x - 2 = 6 -> 4x = 8 -> x = 2 (and it doubles as the excluded value, a real trap here). Dropped 4 (plus one) and -3 (negate). NEW 12: stopping one step early at 4x = 12 and reporting 12. NEW 0: sign error moving the -6 across, x + 3x + 6 = 6 -> 4x = 0 -> x = 0. Remaining relations: 2 -> 3 (plus one) only.

Solution: f(g(a)) = 2(a^2+1) - 3 = 2a^2 - 1 = 17 -> a^2 = 9 -> a = 3. KEPT the original 9 (square) because it is the standard forgot-to-take-the-square-root answer at a^2 = 9. Dropped 2 (minus one) and 4 (plus one). NEW 3.5: composing in the wrong order, g(f(a)) = (2a-3)^2 + 1 = 17 -> (2a-3)^2 = 16 -> 2a-3 = 4 -> a = 3.5. NEW 2.45: subtracting the 3 on the wrong side, 2(a^2+1) = 17-3 = 14 -> a^2 = 6 -> a = 2.45. Remaining relations: 9 = 3^2 only.

Solution: (x+y)^2 = 49 = x^2+y^2+2xy = 29 + 2xy -> 2xy = 20 -> xy = 10. KEPT the original 20 (double) because it is the stop-one-step-early answer: reporting 2xy. Dropped 5 (halve). Solution: y = mx - 4 meets y = x^2 once -> x^2 - mx + 4 = 0 with m^2 - 16 = 0 -> m = 4 (positive branch, first quadrant). KEPT the original 16 (square) because it is the forgot-the-square-root answer at m^2 = 16. Dropped 2 (halve), which was also the tangency x-coordinate and so doubly tempting as a hub. KEPT 4.33, which was not slip-derived: it is the secant slope from (0,-4) to a guessed contact point (3,9), (9+4)/3 = 4.33. NEW 2.83: mis-deriving the tangent line at (a,a^2) as y = 2ax - 2a^2, so 2a^2 = 4, a = 1.414, m = 2a = 2.83. Remaining relations: 16 = 4^2 only.

Solution: roots r and 2r, sum 3r = 12 -> r = 4, product k = r(2r) = 2(16) = 32. KEPT the original 36, which was not slip-derived and is the best error here: reading 'one solution is twice the other' as a double root, x = 6, k = 36. Dropped 16 (halve) and 64 (double). NEW 128: using the root-difference/discriminant route, (r)^2 = 144 - 4k, but dropping the 4: 16 = 144 - k -> k = 128. NEW 4: solving for the wrong quantity and reporting the smaller root r = 4 instead of k. Remaining relations: none.

Solution: x^2 = 4 or 9 -> x = 2,-2,3,-3 -> product = (2)(-2)(3)(-3) = 36. KEPT the original 6 (sqrt) because it is the real error of multiplying only the positive roots, 2*3 = 6. dx=15, dy=20, distance=25. Kept '625' (computed 15^2+20^2=625 and forgot the square root) as the single relation - the most common slip on distance problems. Dropped '5' (sqrt of the key). Central angle 80 -> inscribed angle 40. Kept '80°' (central angle used directly) as the single relation. Legs 15 and 36 -> hypotenuse sqrt(225+1296)=sqrt(1521)=39. x^2+y^2-6x+8y-11=0 -> (x-3)^2+(y+4)^2 = 11+9+16 = 36, r=6. Kept '36' (stopped at r^2, forgot the square root) as the single relation. New: √14 - sign error while completing the square, r^2 = 9+16-11 = 14 (subtracting the constant instead of moving it across). Remaining relation count: 1 (36 = 6^2).

Hypotenuse 41, leg 9 -> AB = sqrt(1681-81) = sqrt(1600) = 40. Kept '50' - flagged as 90-40, but its real source is 41+9=50, adding the two given lengths. Retained '32' (=41-9, subtracting lengths instead of squares), which is not slip-derived. Dropped '41' (plus one / copying the hypotenuse). New: 41.98 = sqrt(41^2+9^2)=sqrt(1762), adding the squares instead of subtracting - i.e. treating AC as a leg. Remaining relation count: 1 (50 = 90-40).

Tangent: PT = sqrt(41^2-9^2) = sqrt(1600) = 40. Kept '50' - flagged as 90-40, but really 41+9, adding the radius to the centre distance. Retained '√1762' (=sqrt(41^2+9^2), adding the squares), not slip-derived. Dropped '41' (plus one / copying the given distance). New: 32 = 41-9, subtracting the lengths rather than the squares. Remaining relation count: 1 (50 = 90-40).

x^2+y^2-6x+8y+9=0 -> (x-3)^2+(y+4)^2 = -9+9+16 = 16, r=4. Kept '16' (stopped at r^2) as the single relation. Retained '5.83' (=sqrt(34), sign error giving r^2 = 9+16+9), not slip-derived. Dropped '5' (plus one). New: 9.54 = sqrt(91) - forgot to halve the linear coefficients, giving (x-6)^2+(y+8)^2 and r^2 = 36+64-9 = 91. Remaining relation count: 1 (16 = 4^2).

Legs 10 and 24 -> hypotenuse 26; the median from the right angle is half the hypotenuse = 13. Kept '26' (gave the hypotenuse itself, the error the item is built to catch). Retained '9.23' (=10*24/26, the altitude to the hypotenuse rather than the median), not slip-derived. Dropped '6.5' (halve). New: 17 = (10+24)/2, averaging the legs instead of halving the hypotenuse. Same circle: r^2 = -9+9+16 = 16, r=4. Kept '16' (stopped at r^2). Retained '√34' (sign error, r^2 = 9+16+9), not slip-derived. Dropped '5' (plus one). New: √91 - did not halve the linear coefficients, so r^2 = 36+64-9 = 91. Remaining relation count: 1 (16 = 4^2).

Tangent: PT = sqrt(15^2-9^2) = sqrt(144) = 12. Kept '6' - flagged as halve, but its real source is 15-9=6, subtracting the lengths instead of the squares, which is the error students actually make. Retained '√306' (=sqrt(15^2+9^2), added the squares), not slip-derived. Dropped '24' (double / 15+9). New: 7.2 = 9*12/15, the altitude from T to OP - the value a student gets after drawing the perpendicular from the point of tangency and stopping one step early. Remaining relation count: 1 (6 = 12/2).

Same circle: r^2 = -9+9+16 = 16, r=4. Kept '16' (stopped at r^2). Retained '√34' (sign error, r^2 = 9+16+9), not slip-derived. Dropped '5' (plus one). New: √43 - halved only the y-coefficient, giving (x-6)^2+(y+4)^2 and r^2 = 36+16-9 = 43. Remaining relation count: 1 (16 = 4^2).

Central angle 100 -> inscribed angle 50. Kept '100°' (central angle used directly) as the single relation. Retained '60°', which was not slip-derived. Dropped '40°' (=90-50). Answer: 0.8^1=.8, ^2=.64, ^3=.512, ^4=.4096, so year 4 is the first below 0.5. KEPT the original '3' (minus-one) because it is the genuine error on this problem: 0.8^3 = 0.512 is so close to 0.5 that a student who rounds, or who stops at the first value that 'looks like about half', answers 3; it is also the floor of the exact log solution ln0.5/ln0.8 = 3.106. Dropped '2' (halve) and '5' (plus one). NEW '1': a student who reads 'multiplied by 0.8' as 'reduced BY 80%', i.e. multiplied by 0.2 — 0.2 of the initial amount is already below half after the first year. (Same value comes from inverting the log ratio: log0.8/log0.5 = 0.32, rounded up to 1.) NEW '7': the decimal/place-value path — starting from 100 units and subtracting 8 per year instead of 20% of the running amount: 100 - 8n < 50 gives n > 6.25, so n = 7. Relations remaining in the set: only 3<->4 (plus one).

The prompt is truncated at the stated mean, but the mean must be 6.4: with f sixes the mean is (78+6f)/(12+f), and 6.4 is the only tidy value that yields the given key (f=3 -> 96/15 = 6.4; f=2 -> 6.4286, f=4 -> 6.375). KEPT the original '4' (plus one), because it is reachable by a real path and not only by the slip: if a student attaches the unknown frequency to the wrong score — f students at 5 and the 4 students at 6 — then (5f+24+42+16)/(12+f) = 6.4 gives 5.2 = 1.4f, f = 3.71, which rounds to 4. Dropped '2' (minus one) and '6' (double). NEW '15': the student who solves for the TOTAL number of students N instead of f — 6.4N = 78 + 6(N-12) -> 0.4N = 6 -> N = 15 — and reports that. NEW '17': the deviation/balance method with the score-5 group left out: deviations from 6.4 are +0.6 x 6 (the sevens) + 1.6 x 2 (the eights) = 6.8, balanced against -0.4 per six, so f = 6.8/0.4 = 17. Relations remaining: only 3<->4 (plus one).

Answer: 240 miles total in 3 + 2 = 5 hours = 48 mph. KEPT the original '24' (halve) because on this problem it is the single most common real error, arriving two ways: dividing only ONE leg's 120 miles by the total 5 hours, and using the harmonic-mean formula without the factor 2 (40x60/(40+60) = 24). Dropped '96' (double) and '100' (sum of the two speeds). NEW '50': the naive arithmetic mean (40+60)/2 — the error the whole item is built to punish, and a value the original set was missing. NEW '52': weighting the speeds by the times but attaching each time to the wrong leg — 3 hours at 60 and 2 hours at 40 gives (180+80)/5 = 52 mph. Relations remaining: only 24<->48 (halve); 50 and 52 are unrelated to everything (50's double, 100, is gone).

Answer: 11:00 p.m. to 9:00 a.m. is 10 hours = two 5-hour doublings backward, so 3,200 / 4 = 800. KEPT the original '1600' (double) — the student who correctly works backward but applies only one doubling period instead of two. KEPT the original '640', which was never slip-derived: it is 3,200 / 5, dividing by the number of hours in a period rather than by 2 per period. Dropped '400' (halve, i.e. three doublings). NEW '12800': the direction reversal — the student who counts the two 5-hour periods correctly but multiplies forward instead of backward, 3,200 x 4 = 12,800, treating the earlier time as the later one. Relations remaining: only 800<->1600 (double); 640 and 12800 are unrelated to any pair (640's x10 = 6,400 and half = 320 are absent; 12,800 is 8x/16x/20x the others, none of which are listed operations).

Answer: noon to 6 a.m. the next day is 18 hours = three 6-hour doublings, 500 x 8 = 4,000. KEPT the original '2000' (halve) — the student who miscounts the elapsed time as 12 hours (noon to midnight, or 'half a day') and applies two doublings. KEPT the original '4500', which was not slip-derived and now has a clean story: 500 x 2^3 = 4,000 plus the original 500 added back in. Dropped '8000' (double, the fencepost error of counting four doublings). NEW '1500': linear instead of exponential growth — 18/6 = 3 periods, so the population is multiplied by 3 rather than by 2^3, giving 500 x 3 = 1,500. Relations remaining: only 2000<->4000 (halve); 1,500 and 4,500 are 3x values, which is not a listed operation.
